content:
Jimmy Kimmel continues to mock Trump for his ongoing efforts to add his name to the Kennedy Center.

"Yesterday, Trump handpicked a Kennedy Center board that voted to suspend renovations—just shortly after a judge ruled they could not add Trump's name to the building without congressional approval," Kimmel said during his Wednesday night monologue.

"So this big baby says if the Supreme Court doesn't overturn that ruling and put his name on the wall next to Kennedy's, no renovations will happen at all," the late-night host added.

Kimmel said the president wants to put his name on "everything in town".

"At this point, the only thing he doesn't want to put his name on is for his son—Don Jr.," Kimmel said of the president's eldest son.

He then joked that Trump had "taken the whole building hostage". He also said: "They really should rename it the Melania Trump Kennedy Center," drawing laughter from the audience.

Trump wrote on Truth Social that he would close the center "for safety reasons" after a federal judge rejected his attempt to add the pretentious phrase "Renovated and Restored by President Trump" to the building's exterior.

Trump wrote in his Tuesday post: "The renovation and reconstruction work is a very large and complex project, and it cannot proceed until the D.C. Circuit Court rules on the board-approved name change," then made his position perfectly clear.

"If the ruling is negative—and it shouldn't be—without being overturned by the U.S. Supreme Court, the Kennedy Center's reconstruction and renovation work will not proceed," he said.

The late President John F. Kennedy's niece, Maria Shriver, had plenty to say about Trump's attempt to permanently associate his name with that of her late uncle.

Shriver wrote on X earlier this week: "I cannot believe what Trump is saying." "A sitting president who won't do any renovations to a public building unless he can put his name on it first... it's a sad state of society, it's really a tragedy."

She criticised Trump as "small-minded" and "narcissistic," adding that "truly great people, those devoted to public service and the public interest, do not behave this way".

She said: "Imagine spending your time and energy on this stuff, while ordinary Americans struggle every day over healthcare, gas, rent and food." "Imagine spending your days on this stuff, while under your leadership the fires of war are still burning."
